note: The bytes a first view of each route is allowed to fetch. See the header of
scripts/budget.mjs for exactly what a first view is taken to include.
These are a RATCHET. Every number here was measured from the built tree by
`node scripts/budget.mjs --adopt`; it is lowered when the site gets lighter
and never raised to admit a regression. Cutting the playground's client
island or a font subset should be followed by --adopt, which writes the
smaller numbers back and refuses to write a larger one. Raising a ceiling is
a decision about what this publication asks a reader to download: it is made
by hand, in a review, with the reason in the commit message, never by a tool
reporting what the tree happens to weigh today.
`match` is first-match-wins in this order and `*` stands for one path
segment, so exact routes come before globs. A route matching no row fails the
build: a new section states its weight rather than inheriting a neighbour's.
`grain` is the slack: an adopted ceiling is the measurement plus at least
one grain, rounded to a multiple of it, so editing a paragraph never fails a
build. It is well under the smallest regression worth catching, which the
table this gate prints on every build names: a client island or a font subset.
